To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vaccination with apolipoprotein-B100 related antigens is a promising strategy to induce atheroproteciton in experimental models of atherosclerotic disease.
atherosclerosis is an immunoinflammatory disease and that immunization against atherosclerotic autoantigens may emerge as an effective therapeutic strategy.

the innate and adaptive immunity plays a role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and that active immunization with specific antigens may represent a novel therapeutic paradigm in the treatment of atherosclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of specific antigens, which may be used for the development of novel immunomodulatory therapies for atherosclerosis.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies based on the induction of immune responses that are atheroprotecting.
identifying and characterizing novel immunoreactive epitopes in atherogenic proteins and with the development of atheroprotecive vaccines against atherogenic proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune response plays a role in atheroprotections and atherosclerosis.
vaccination against specific atherogenic antigens may be a promising novel therapeutic strategy to prevent and treat atherosclerosis.
the immune response to atherogenic lipoproteins is complex and multifactorial and that the role of the immune response in atherogenesis is not fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease and that vaccination may be an attractive therapeutic strategy to modulate the atherosclerotic immune response.
the immune system can be harnessed to protect against atherogenesis and that vaccination may emerge as a viable strategy to achieve this.
the innate and adaptive immunity plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of immune responses against specific autoantigens may emerge as an important new therapeutic strategy in the management of atherosclerosis.
the immune system can be manipulated to induce atherosclerosis, and that the induction of atheroprotecitve immune responses can be achieved.
atheroprotectiveness of vaccination is not limited to a single antigen but is rather a function of the type and magnitude of immune responses elicited by vaccination.
